The Stone Cage Mountains are a small mountain range at the western end of the Shadowcrag Mountains, separating the Demon Wastes from Eldeen Reaches.The Lake of Fire is the mouth of a massive volcano, said to be the prison of a powerful fiend. The crater of this volcano extends almost a full mile. Legends say there are powerful treasures in the lake, or that some magic wielders can draw their powers from it. A channel north of the Wastes, separating the land from the islands, as well as connecting the Seas.
a legendary cave buried deep below the Wastes in Khyber. It is said to be filled with Khyber dragonshards that contain countless souls within them. It is a manifest zone to Dolurrh, which causes all souls who die there to be trapped within the dragonshards.
During the imprisonment of Khyber, he spawned unimaginable horrors called fiends, that surged through the world through cracks and volcanic eruptions. Not long after creation, the fiends overran the world, entering the Age of Demons.
During the war that ended the Age of Demons, lesser fiends escaped to the region of the Demon Wastes.
Under Galifar, little attention was payed to the Demon Wastes. It was treated as if it simply didn't exist.
Two major barbarian cultures exist in The Wastes. The Ghaash'kala clans reside within The Labyrinth, while Carrion Tribes scattered across the land still worship the imprisoned demonic Overlords.Cities
Ashtakala Blood Crescent
Desolate Fiendfell Festering Holt Ghaash Dar Maruk Dar Rotting Blade
The unofficial capital of the Demon Wastes. This is the home of the most powerful of the fiends from the Age of Demons. Ashtakala is the home of the Lords of Dust. This city lies in the center of an ever raging sandstorm, day and night. This Magical maelstrom serves two purposes: to channel spells preventing divination and teleportation, and serves as a defense system. Those who can penetrate the storm will find a basalt and brass city created thousands of years ago. The entire city is cloaked in magic, conforming everything that enters or exists in the city to conform to the look and feel of the ancient demons. This city acts as a contained slice of history.
A famously cursed settlement on the eastern edge of the Wastes. It is formerly known as Greenholt, Newholt, and Kymar's Folly. It has changed hands numerous times, having had a string of odd occurances. At first, Aundair tried to build a settlement, and then Thrane began to build a hermitage, and, finally, House Lyrandar attempted to establish an enclave at that site. In all three cases, the entire population of the city would vanish overnight, without taking their belongings, not a trace of them remained. Now, it is called Desolate, and no settlers currently inhabit it.

A group primarily composed of orcs, as well as half-orcs, and humans. They are split into four clans, each that inhabit and protect a different section of The Labyrinth. Each clan has two leaders, the kizshmit, the military leader, and the sar'malaan, the spiritual leader or high priest. They all worship Kalok Shash, and fight to contain the evils of the Demon Wastes in The Labyrinth. The Jaasakah clan inhabits the eastern Labyrinth and guards the lands to the east. The Kastar clan inhabits the western Labyrinth and guards the lands to the west.
The Maruk Clan is one of the oldest clans, and inhabit central Labyrinth. They guard the main passages used by the Rakasha of the Lords of Dust to escape the Wastes. they are trained to spot deceptions and see through disguises. They have the highest percentages of Human and Half-Orc members. The Vaanka clan inhabits the northwest region of the Labyrinth and protects the entrances from there.
Savage, human barbarian tribes that dwell in the Wastes. These tribes often worship demons, each tribe worshipping different Overlords. These tribes are nomadic, and only use stone-age technology. They practice ritual scarification.

item.title: The Labyrinth
item.description:
The most efficient way to travel into the Demon Wastes. It is heavily guarded by The Ghaash'kala, an orcish group whos purpose is to keep the evils of the Wastes from escaping.The Labyrinth is a large maze of winding canyons and caverns. The air is dry, and hot.
After the end of the Age of Demons, the Ghaash'kala formed in the Labyrinth to keep the horrors within from spreading, and to keep any brave enough to venture in safe.
There are said to be portals to Khyber in the Labyrinth.

item.title: Changeling
item.description:
Col “I will protect your children if they follow my path. Let them wander the world. They may be shunned and feared, but they will never be destroyed.” Jes agreed, and the traveler gave her his cloak. When she draped it over her children, their old faces melted away and they could be whoever they wanted to be. And so it remains. Though the children are shunned by all, the gift of the Traveler protects them still.
About 1300 years ago in early Khorvaire, the leaders of the precursor nations of Cyre, Karrnath, and Thrane launched a genocidal attack against changelings within their borders. This forced many to flee to the precursor lands of Aundair and Breland to live in secrecy.
Long after, a changeling known as Kel become unhappy with the constant hiding the changelings were forced into. He missioned across Khorvaire to find other changeling covens, and began a gradual migration to the Lhazaar Principalities before settling on Lastpoint.
There is speculation that changelings resulted from the interbreeding of humans and doppelgangers. As the offspring evolved, they formed into their own distinct race.
Another popular theory is that changelings originated first, and doppelgangers were modeled after their talents.
Another belief states that the first changeling, tiefling, and skulk bloodlines began amongst the sages of the kingdom of Ohr Kaluun, by making body altering pacts will fell beings.
Some changeling priests tell a faithful story about a woman named Jes, with 100 children. In times of trouble, she sought an audience with the Sovereign Host, but was met with silence. Eventually, a lone traveler came and promised to protect Jes' children, only if they followed the travelers path. Accepting Jes, she was given a cloak that she spread over her hundred children. Though their former faces melted away, they had the ability to look like whoever they wanted, becoming the changeling race.
Others speculate that this traveler channeled his will and desires into doppelgangers to create a new race for an unknown purpose.
Finally, some believe changelings to be a magical manifestation starting in the Feywild.
In their natural form, they look human, but appear faded or lacking detail, like an unfinished painting. They appear to have a gray, gauzy extra layer of skin over their bodies. Their skin tone is pale, typically white or light grey, and their hair is thin and fair, commonly silver-white, platinum blond, with some traces of green, pink, or blue. They have blank, colorless eyes that appear sunken. Their other features are barely noticeable, and typically expressionless. They typically stand at 5-6ft, and are usually frail and gangly bodied. Most changelings adopt a few personas to serve them in different times of need. They can be of any moral stance, but many face pragmatic neutrality, worrying about their own needs and issues. They are largely uninterested in social interactions. They believe that life is short, and they should make the most of it. A changeling will not "make do", they will maximize their current experience, and try to live a most leisurely life. These creatures excel at learning new languages, and have an appreciation for magic and technology similar to their powers.

A location on the world of Eberron

There are 5 official nations of Khorvaire, although there are many more areas to this continent. The nations include Aundair, Breland, Karrnath, Thrane, and the Mournland.
Other bordered lands in Khorvaire include The Demon Wastes, the Shadow Marches, Droaam, Eldeen Reaches, Zilargo, Darguun, the Talenta Plains, Q'Barra, Valenar, Mror Holds, and the coast of the Lhazaar Principalities.Islands

Khorvaire is located in the northern hemisphere on Eberron. It neighbors the Bitter Seato the north, the Lhazaar Sea to the east, the Barren Seato the west, and the Thunder Seato the south. The landscape varies greatly, from wastelands and mountains to the north, to jungles and deserts in the south.TBA
While not native to Khorvaire, humans dominate the continent. Humans founded the Five Nations. The largest populations can be found in Aundair, Breland, Karrnath, The Lhazaar Principalities, and Thrane.
Along with humans, dwarves are also migrants to Khorvaire. Dwarves orignally migrated to the Mror Holds, far before the arrival of humanity. Large dwarven settlements can be found there, however there are some that can be found in other various parts of Khorvaire. The crafty dwarves founded the House Kundarak to manage banking and financial institutes.
Elves are also non native to Khorvaire. They can currently be found in several main locations across Khorvaire:
Aerenal: These elves hailed from the island subcontinent with the same name. There are no large settlements of Aerenal elves, however they can be found in small numbers near nearly every city.
Valenar: These elves , more specifically Tairnadal, hail in the nation of Valenar.
Phiarlan and Thuranni: These elves make up two dragonmark houses, and can be found wherever their enclaves are.
Gnomes are native to Zilargo, but can be found throughout the continent. The Gnomish House Sivis works in diplomacy and communications, helping keep the greater society of Khorvaire intact.
The goblinoids are composed of 3 main races: Goblins, hobgoblins, and bugbears. These races once dominated the continent of Khorvaire, due to their origins there. While many no longer have control over the continent, some are attempting to rebuild in Darguun. Many goblinoids can also be found in the nation of Droaam. Goblins exist as an underclass in most cities, while hobgoblins and bugbears are employed as mercenaries for the House of Deneith.
Half Elves are common in Khorvaire as a distinct race, known as the Khoravar due to their Khorvairian origins. Many are associated with the Dragonmark Houses of House Medani and [House [Lyrandar]].
Halflings are native to the Talenta Plains. These halflings tend to be very traditional, and tribal.
Orcs and their progeny, half-orcs, inhabit the western parts of Khorvaire, and have so for a millennia. They can primarily be found in the Shadow Marches, Demon Wastes, and Droaam.

The Towering Wood is a dense, ancient forest home to the many tribes of shifters and Druidic Circles. This forest is vast, and mainly untamed. The Wardens of the Wood operate out of this forest, but only out of a small portion. The fey presence is strong here, often creating manifest zones tied to Thelanis.
Located in the northwest corner of The Towering Wood, The Twilight Demesne is a manifest zone for the realm of Thelanis.
The heart of the Towering Wood, these awakened trees are large, and tower over all the others. It is believed that these trees were the first trees ever made on Eberron.
Druids and shifters had called the region of the Eldeen Reaches home for thousands of years. Originally, the eastern part of the Reaches was claimed by Aundair. However, during The Last War, Aundair reduced their focus of this area, ignoring the banditry plaguing the farmers inhabiting the land. Eventually the druids came to the aid of these farmers, causing the people of eastern Aundair to secede and form The Eldeen Reaches, a nation that would be recognized by the Treaty of ThroneholdThere are two main groups of civilizations located in Eldeen Reaches. They seek to protect wildlife and consider most aspects of modern society to be a threat to the wildlands. They ideally avoid bloodshed, but some more extreme members consider acts of terrorism to prove their point.
This small druidic sect heavily embraces death and decay as a part of the natural cycle. These druids seek to preserve the cycle of life and death, and restore the balance between the two. They are willing to use disease and death to clear out the week in order to create room for new life. They seek to either prevent or advance a coming cataclysm they call "Winter". The majority of the population that makes up the Children of Winter are humans, the rest being shifters. These druids are fascinating with the Day of Mourning, and left the The Towering Wood to study it, and aid in bringing the age to an end. The Children base out of The Gloaming.
The Gatekeepers are the oldest druid sect in Khorvaire, mostly made up of Orcs, half-orcs, and later shifters. These druids were heavily decimated during the invasions of the Daelkyr. Their main task was to defend nature against aberrations, outsiders, undead, and other unnatural beings.

item.title: House Orien
item.description:
Infobox
The Orien dragonmark first appeared in Aundair 1900 years ago. Most humans that developed this mark were among travelers, merchants, and teamsters. Initially, each marked human competed against each other before eventually realizing their power united. The newly established House Orien started to focus on transportation, and caravans to transport and deliver goods across Khorvaire. Orien sought to create safe passage for their caravans, and used their political diplomacy to create better roads. Before the invention of the Speaking Stone, Orien ran a nationwide postal service. Lightning Rail:
in 811yk, House Cannith created the first lightning rail, and the elemental binders of Zilargo powered it. Eventually Orien began to involve itself with the lightning rail, taking control of it and its spread.
House Orien is led by Baron Kwanti d'Orien, patriarch.
House Orien is by far the most diverse among the houses. Although humans are the only race that can carry the dragonmark, many other races are involved in House Orien, such as Half-Elf (Khoravar), Half-Orc, and even changelings and shifters. House Orien encourages its members to have large families, and even accepts children out of wedlock as fully fledged scions. House Orien controls both the Couriers Guild as well as the Transportation Guild. The Couriers guild is tasked with the delivery of goods and small parcels, while the transportation guild is in charge of maintaining trade routes and operating the lightning rail. Orien also runs a teleportation business, however it is very experimental and the risk factors often deter business.Orien has recently introduced Splendor Caravans, luxury horse-drawn carriages. While slower than the lightning rail, the Caravans often make excellent travel for short distances, as well as areas where the lightning rail is in repair.

item.title: Xoriat
item.description:
The Realm of Madness
Xoriat is one of the many planar realms of Eberron. It is a realm of constantly changing madness and illusions, and all who enter are driven mad. Time is processed differently in Xoriat, some theorizing that you could enter the past through it.
The Daelkyr originate from Xoriat, and are the lords of the realm. Many creatures serve the Daelkyr, some created by them. These include the illithid, ethergaunt, beholders, grick, and many other aberrations.
Nine thousand years ago, the planar incursion of Xoriat began. The Daelkyr began invading Eberron through the Shadow Marches, with intent to subjugate Eberron to the same madness of their own plane. Recently, a portal has been rumored to have opened in the Eldeen Reaches.

item.title: Draconic Prophecy
item.description:
For days, she had watched the signs appear in the heavens, cross-referencing the omens with the Codex of Alaraxus and the movement of smoke and water. This was the final piece in the puzzle. The Lord of Fire would rise again in the City of Illusions, and only three could return him to his prison: the child of storms, the shaper of steel, and the hand of the Keeper. Tonight she would head to Khorvaire; tomorrow she would begin the search for her soldiers of destiny.
There is no defined origin or creator of the Draconic Prophecy, but many speculate it was created by the Progenitor Dragons. This ancient force transcends history, shaping the destiny of Eberron|Eberron.
The Draconic Prophecy reveals itself in various different ways around the world. From the stars to the moon, clouds, mountain ridges, trees, rivers, and especially Dragonmarks borne by certain humanoids.
The blue dragon Ourelonastrix and the coatl Hezcalipa first discovered the prophecys potential and used its knowledge to lead the Dragons and Coatls in their war against the Overlords. However, this did not pan out how they had hoped.
The Draconic Prophecy is very difficult to transcribe and read, typically. The Dragons of Argonnessen observe and record every sign of the draconic prophecy. This includes the positions of the moon, stars, the position of The Ring of Siberys, and physical manifestations of Dragonmarks. Creatures with the longest lifespans, such as Dragons, Aerenal elves, and other immortal beings have the ability and patience to truly understand the prophecy.
The followers of Thir believe the prophecy is a recollection of creation itself. To them, they are to observe the natural happenings of the prophecy as it writes its own destiny in real time.
The Chamber believes that the prophecy can be used to shape the future. They believe it is a tool or a guide, and the Dragons play a key role.
The Lords of Dust: seek to use the prophecy to free their ancient masters. They are experts in twisting the prophecy to their advantage, purposely setting events into motion that might one day lead to the return of the Overlords.

The Deep Mine is a platinum mine set in the northeastern part of Zilargo, in the Seawall Mountains. The Deep Mine is host to the most sophisticated mining team, a collaboration between the Dragonmark Houses and the Dwarvish clan Mroranon. Moranon provides most of the labor, mining the pure platinum and smelting it into perfect ingots. House Kundarak will purchase the ingots, using them as internal currency. These mines have been known to disturb the monsters of Khyber, and attract the attention of thieves and bandits. Therefore, House Kundarak provides great levels of security. House Sivis handles relations between the working forces of the Mine and the goverment of Zilargo.
Zilargo was inhabited by the gnomes for thousands of years, well into the Dhakaani Empire and Daelkyr War. At one point, Zilargo was taken over by the Dhakaani Empire, however the gnomes quickly reclaimed their territory during the Daelkyr War. From the ashes of the collapse of the Dhakaani Empire rose 3 gnomish city-states: Korranberg, Trolanport and Zolanberg.
Eventually these city-states became under attack from Maellon the Reaver and Karrn the Conquerer, forcing them to innovate to survive. The gnomes built their first form of government, the democracy of The Triumvirate, and the nation of Zilargo. The Trust was also created as a secret body of police to protect the nation.
During the reign of Galifar ir'Wynarn I., Zilargo surrendered to his subjugation and negotiated the status of an independant province to the Kingdom of Galifar. During the first part of The Last War, Zilargo remained loyal to the Kingdom of Galifar. However their political stance changed in 962 YK for an unknown reason, declaring itself loyal to Breland.
In 996 YK, the Treaty of Thronehold declared Zilargo a recognized nation of Khorvaire.The people of Zilargo are thirsty for knowledge, from the secrets of the universe to the juiciest gossip. Their desire for knowledge creates a environment filled with deceit, blackmail, deals, and manipulation.

As the oldest city of Zilargo, Korranberg is home to the vaunted Library of Korranberg, which is arguably the greatest collection of knowledge on the world of Eberron, and is amongst the best universities. Both House Orien Trade Routes and the lightning rain pass through here. Korranberg is also a central point to The Triumvirate, which originally rules from Trolanport. The city itself is administered by a Council of Nine, where the city's triumvir is chosen. House Sivis most ancient enclave resides here.
The Labyrinth is the head enclave for House Sivis. This historical enclave was built directly above the many cavernous tunnels used by the Dhakaani Empire. Today, these caverns are host to the many vaults used by House Sivis, holding records of vital communications.
A city host to the House Orien trade route, approximately halfway between Trolanport and Oskilor.
A large port town in the center of Zilargo. Oskilor lies on the House Orien trade route. The Sharn Inquisitive recieves intel from.
A cillage in central Zilargo. It lies on the crossing of both House Orien trade routes that pass through the nation.
The capital city of Zilargo, built next to the Trolan River. Trolanport was build on the ruined foundations of the Dhakaani Empire. The port is designed with a canal system, and is the central hub for gnomish shipbuilding of both naval and aerial types. Trolanport a central trade point of Khorvaire, and is a major departure port for Xen'drik. Aerenal, and Sarlona. While all Dragonmark Houses have presence in Trolanport, House Kundarak, House Sivis, and House Cannith have major enclaves here.
A small city in the Seawall Mountains, known for its mining operations. Zolanberg is one of the three major cities that make up The Triumvirate. This city hosts both the Orien Trade Route and the lightning rail. Zolanberg is governed by a Council of Nine, whos representatives are pulled from the wealthy elite. It is within this council that the triumvir of Zolanberg is chosen. House Kundarak has a major presence, including a large vault. House Tharashk also has a Prospectors Guild vault located here.

The most widely read source written in all of Khorvaire, and perhaps all of Eberron. The paper originated in Zilargo, and has worked hard to maintain a reputation of neutrality and objectivity. It is printed in Korranberg, but covers news from all over Khorvaire.
The Chronicle heavily covered the peace process during the end of The Last War, and is held in contempt by King Kaius III of Karrnath. He blames the Chronicle for a number of setbacks he suffered, and thus many reporters face harassment when operating in Karrnath. Similar grievances are held by the Boromar Clan and House Thuranni.
The Library of Korranberg is a research library standing as the largest repository of knowlegde in Khorvaire. The library's buildings take up a quarter of the city of Korranberg, and is a great source of gnomish pride. The library also has eight colleges, each focusing on a particular field of study that attracts students from across the continent. The library is constantly expanding as it gathers more knowledge and improves its resources.
The Library was founded by Loremaster Dorius Alyre ir'Korran long before the founding of the Kingdom of Galifar. Dorius was an adherent to the belief that deities of the Sovereign Host were dragons that ascended to godhood, and thus created the library in hope that he himself might ascent to take the place of Aureon. His family and the city-states of Zilargo supported his efforts, intrigued by the idea of having the greatest library in the world. The Trust is tasked with guarding the library.The Library is run by a central council made up of the doyens of the eight colleges of the library. The head of the council is always an appointed member of the Korran family, currently held by Alina Alrene ir'Korran. The eight colleges and their subjects are:
Aureon's Holt (law and oratory)
Balinor's Horn (natural sciences) Blackdragon (alchemy) Drystone (engineering) Lyrris (art and literature) Morridan (mathematics) Soladas (history) The Tabernacle (religion and philosophy)
The governing body of Zilargo. It was originally formed to govern the Library of Korranberg, but was chosen as the general form of government to unite the original three city-states of Zilargo against Maellon the Reaver. The Triumvirate is composed of three Triumvir chosen from Korranberg, Trolanport, and Zolanberg. Most Triumvirs are chosen from the Council of Nine, the local government of each city.
A national, non-military organization charged with the safety and security of Zilargo. The Trust acts as a secret police, often dressing in plain clothing and acting like regular folk, while their head is on swivel for any crime or conspiracy. The Trust acknowledges the shared virtues of ingenuity, curiosity, love of family, and overcoming adversity through wit and wisdom. The Trust has jurisdiction over punishing those it determines guilty of transgression, and the justice is swift and merciless. There is no court of law, and any Zil citizen could be an agent of The Trust without anyone knowing. Because of this, Zilargo has the lowest crime rate in all of Khorvaire.
The security agency began in Korranberg as an outgrowth of the Korranberg Library. The founder of the organization is only remembered by her title of "The Proctor", and all leaders since have gone by this title.Although the gnomes allied with each other, this did not stop the feud between and within the different city-states. The Trust was created in order to keep the nation straight and together. Each of the three Triumvirs was given the power to select agents from their city to create this secret agency. The Trust soon secured total control over law enforcement and national security in Zilargo.

item.title: Eberron
item.description:
The World of Eberron
The world of Eberron is composed of 7 different continents. Khorvaire is the most diverse continent, and had hosted The Last War. Aerenal is an island continent that lies to the southeast of Khorvaire. Xen'drik is south of Khorvaire, and is home to ancient magic. Sarlona lies west, the original home of humans. Argonnessen is known for its dragons and barbarian human tribes. Frostfell is a landmass located north of Khorvaire, and is a region of ice and snow. The last, Everice, is a shifting sheet of ice located south of Xen'drik. The subterranean continent is known as Khyber.

Eberron was the name of one of the founding dragons of Eberron, or also known as a member of the Progenitor Dragons. Eberron created the world with a noble sacrifice, and was hence then named after her.
Eberron was one of three siblings. She had one sister, Khyber, and one brother, Siberys.

item.title: Progenitor Dragons
item.description:
And thus rose the dawn of Eberron > The World
The Progenitor Dragons consist of three siblings: Khyber, Eberron, and Siberys.
For some malevolent reason, Khyber murdered her brother Siberys. To contain the evil, Eberron used her own body as a prison to contain Khyber. The blood of Siberys spilt over Eberron, creating the first life, Dragons. Siberys' blood was also used to independantly create Coatls. His scales created the cosmos, and whats now known as The Ring of Siberys.

item.description:

Physical manifestations of the Draconic Prophecy that appear as unique, natural marks on certain bloodlines.
Dragonmarks are physical manifestations of the Draconic Prophecy, and typically appear on certain bloodlines of Khorvaire. They can appear at random, sometimes creating an Aberrant Dragonmark. Dragonmarks are physical marks, more intricate than a birthmark and more distinct than a tattoo. As the wearer ages, and the dragonmark gains power, it will start to expand in size and complexity while keeping the same general shape and idea. Dragonmarks vary in patterns and color, depending on the house and the wearer.There are four different types of marks. Lesser, Greater, Siberys, and Aberrant. Fact
The Draconic Prophecy reads that, because there are thirteen moons of Eberron, the perfect number of dragonnmarks is thirteen.
Lesser marks are typically the first marks to appear when a creature reaches adolescence. These are the simplest forms of the mark, and offer the lowest form of magic. These can be studied and focused on to create Greater Marks.

Greater marks are often results of an expanding and growing lesser mark. These marks offer a greater power, with less understanding. Most average mark wearers will reach their full potential with a greater mark.

Siberys marks are the rarest mark, and the final form of a dragonmark. Most mark wearers never reach the Siberys evolution, and those who do are said to be descendants of Siberys himself.
Aberrant dragonmarks can appear on any race, and are the most dangerous mark form. The most common way to manifest an aberrant mark is for two different dragonmarked families to have a child. This union is forbidden by The Twelve.
Before the formation of Galifar, aberrant marks were much more common. The first Sharn was destroyed with an earthquake by the powers of an aberrant leader. In an effort to eradicate dangerous individuals, the dragonmarked houses united in the War of the Mark and hunted down all aberrant marks, significantly reducing the numbers of those which such marks. Present day, aberrants are no longer hunted down and killed, but most dragonmarks fear the aberrants, and will not hesitate to take them out.

item.title: Deep Gnome
item.description:
Col A subrace of gnomes that inhabit Khyber, enslaved during the Daelkyr War.

These gnomes were subjugated and enslaved during the Daelkyr War, damning them to Khyber. These gnomes seek to atone for their heinous crimes, continuing to live deep below Zilargo, too ashamed to live with their surface brethren.
These gnomes have all of the other features of a Gnome, however they posses wiry, rock colored skin and wispy hair.
These gnomes are quite ashamed of their actions during the Daelkyr War, seeking to atone for their misdoings. They believe they are undeserving of a surface life, and choose to dwell in Khyber.

item.title: deep gnome
Khyber
item.description:
Khyber, one of the Progenitor Dragons, killed her brother Siberys, which then caused her sister Eberron, to entrap her and create the world of Eberron.
Khyber has one sister, who also happens to be her keeper, Eberron. She also has a brother who she murdered herself named Siberys.Located deep in the earth, often near layers of Magma. These are living crystals, typically grown on cavern walls. These shards are a deep blue to violet, laced with gleaming veins.Khyber Dragonshards have an affinity for binding magics. they are used for Elemental binding of airships, the lightning rail, and elemental galleons. They are also used for phylacteries, planar binding, and other effects that trap or manipulate spirits. They are also used for many necromancy rituals.
Khyber, the area lying beneath the world of Eberron, was amply named after the great Progenitor Dragon. Most believe that this subterranean world is the body of the dragon. The upper levels of Khyber typically contain the usual amounts of stone and dirt, however the deeper layers often contain a vast array of demiplanes with strange contents.
Khyber hosts a variety of twisted tunnels, caverns, and other natural formations that no being on Eberron could think of fully mapping out. Great chambers host pastures to monsters, while immense chasms shelter forgotten fortresses carved from stone.
Deeper into Khyber lie horrors created by a disastrous epoch from the Age of Demons. Overlords remain imprisoned in dragonshards or arcane cells, while the Daelkyr carve out their own fortresses and kingdoms.
In the deepest reaches of Khyber, reality itself twists, disobeying the physical laws of Eberron. Colors unkown to the human eye glow from mysterious crystals, magma rock flows through rivers that defy physics. Here, the very essence of the world instills madness and wonder.
Passageways to Khyber are rare, but not impossible to find. These passageways are often dangerous, containing a multitude of horrid monsters and reality twisting features. Some say Breland contains at least one passage.

item.title: Half-Orc
item.description:
Col A mix between Human and Orc, Half-Orcs are seen as savages and are heavily looked down upon by the rest of society.

Originally created by the interbreeding of humans and orcs, half-orcs now mainly reside in the Shadow Marches with House Tharashk.
Half-Orcs are a standard divvy between their ancestors. Usually smaller than an Orc, but larger than a Human. They often grow orcish tusks, with skintone ranging from an orcish to human color.
Half-Orcs are generally more tame than their Orc ancestors, however they still maintain enough savagery to illicit discomfort in many of the other species of Eberron.

item.title: House Cannith
item.description:
Infobox
The Cannith Dragonmark first appeared about 2500 years ago, appearing on artisans and craftsmen of ancient Cyre.
Around 1,000 years later, the War of the Mark began with Cannith being an active and enthusiastic participant, having involvement in trade and manufacturing. After the war, Cannith emerged as a super power amongst the houses. They used that influence to bring the houses together to form The Twelve. They allied with the elemental binders of Zilargo and the scions of House Lyrandar to create the first elemental sea vessels. Because of this overwhelming success, Cannith teamed with House Orien to create the lightning rail.
When The Last War broke out, Cannith acted as an arms dealer to all nations. They amassed a great fortune in gold, rivaling that of House Kundarak. The Five Nations became so reliant on Cannith and their weapons, granting them political advantage.
Eventually, Cannith also began supplying soldiers to weild their weapons. The first Warforged marched out of Whitehearth in 965 YK. By the end of the war, Cannith was believed to be the most powerful dragonmarked house.
However on the Day of Mourning, the disaster destroying Cyre would also destroy the Whitehearth forgehold along with its wealth, knowledge, and resources. Many of the house's heirs perished in this phenomenon, notably Baron Starrin d'Cannith,
The death of Starrin d'Cannith caused a succession crisis within Cannith, as his only heir had also perished in the event. With the house in disarray and with so many high-ranking officials suddenly dead, no one still within the house could elect a leader. Three rivals within the house rose to claim the title.
After the Treaty of Thronehold liberated the Warforged, they banned Cannith from creating more. The end of the war came the end of Cannith's role as an international arms dealer, as well as most of their political influence.The leaders of Cannith today have become incredibly determined to restore their power and wealth leading to bitter rivalry amongst the leaders.The ruling leader of Cannith is either a patriarch of matriarch. When the last single Patriarch died, three heirs stepped up to claim the title. None could claim a majority of supporters, so the house split into three factions, each supporting one heir.
Merrix d'Cannith controls Cannith South, and while he is the youngest leader, his rivals are weary of his incredible talents as an artificer.
Jorlanna d'Cannith controls Cannith West, and has the strongest family tie to Starrin d'Cannith. However, Jorlanna is plagued by a scandalous past.
Zorlan d'Cannith controls Cannith East, and is well known for being a prudent businessman. Zorlan has powerful allies in Karrnath, also contributing to his biggest hinderance.
Most members of House Cannith are humans, and only them bear the Mark of Making. House Cannith maintains control over the Fabricators Guild and the Tinkers Guild. Cannith produces mundane fine wares, while crafted with magic, are not magical items. Items created by this house are marked with the houses gorgon symbol.Cannith has also worked with several other houses to create the following: Elemental Airship Elemental Galleon Elemental Land Cart Everbright Lantern Lightning Rail

War of the Mark
item.description:
-1500 - -1497 Most of the historical recollection of the War is told from the perspective of the Dragonmarked Houses, and therefore cannot be 100% accurate accounts.
The War of the Mark was fought between the twelve Dragonmark Houses, and the Aberrant Marks.
Columns Column The Dragonmark Houses feared the devastating power of the
Aberrant Marks, and sought to genocide them. Column Almost if not all Aberrant Marks were destroyed by the houses. They are now often feared and live in secret.
In the third year of the war, Lord Halas Tarkanan began organizing the aberrants into a military force to oppose the houses. He was accompanied by the Lady of Plague. Though she is commonly seen as a monster, historical records say that she loathed using her abilities unless forced. While Tarkanan's efforts extended the conflicts, the aberrants eventually fell. In a final effort, both Tarkanan and Lady of Plague unleashed the power of their marks that ultimately destroyed the city of Sharn.

item.title: Lysse Lyrriman d'Sivis
item.description:
Infobox
Lysse Lyrriman d'Sivis is the Baron and house Matriarch to House Sivis. Lysse has invested much time and money into Tasker's Dream, a project created by Tasker Torralyn d'Sivis to create and improve the communication technology held by the gnomes. Lysse was married to Rhysand Lyrriman d'Sivis before his passing in 994YK. Lysse and Rhysand welcomed their only child, Vendron Lyrriman d'Sivis in 884YK.
Activities: Lysse tends to handle most house concerns from within The Labyrinth in Korranberg.Personality: Lysse is a cunning and masterful negotiator and communicator. She often maintains the traditional business of the house, as well as monitoring the goings of Tasker's Dream.

item.title: House Sivis
item.description:
Infobox The Sivis Dragonmark first appeared about 2800 years ago. The gnomes have carefully cultivated the people around them since that time and have remained neutral in all conflicts.
House Sivis is governed by a high council composed of representation from each of the nations in which the house operates. The council is currently led by Lysse Lyrriman d'Sivis, and has been in her council since the beginning of The Last War.
All members of House Sivis are gnomes, but not all members carry Mark of Scribing. House Sivis maintains control over the Notaries Guild and the Speakers Guild, however members of the guild are not necessarily members of House Sivis. Sivis is based out of Korranberg, however have many enclaves across Khorvaire.

item.title: Zilargo
Gnome
item.description:
Col Gnomes are one of the most inquisitive races, seeking knowlege in all its forms.
The gnomes originate from the plane of Thelanis, inhabiting the various Eladrin feyspires. The Gnomes made quick work of clearing the Kobolds from the land to the north. The Gnomes were known to use guerilla tactics to keep out the invasion of the Dhakaani Empire. However, they did eventually fall and become enslaved to the Goblin Empire. The Gnomes, smarter than the Goblins, were eventually the fall of the Dhakaani Empire by convincing the Goblins to attack each other.
As the Gnomes rose back into power, they divided into many different clans, eventually forming 3 city-states, becoming the first seafaring race of Khorvaire. Many Gnomes were known to befriend humans, and traded much information with them. Eventually House Sivis became the third race to manifest a Dragonmark, The Mark of Scribing.
2,400 years ago, a human warlord named Maellon the Reaver set his sights on the eastern and southern coast of Khorvaire, along with Karrn the Conquerer from the north. The three gnome city-states formed together to create a single nation, Zilargo. Not long after the gnomes continued exploring Khorvaire, even setting to the seas. They tried to start a settlement on Xen'drik, modern day Stormreach. However, the settlement was short lived.
During the reign of Galifar, Galifar ir'Wynarn I. set his sights on Zilargo. THe gnomes met his forces in the valley north of Dragonroost and immediately surrendered. The gnomes agreed to remain a sovereign principality of the nation of Galifar, and swore allegiance to the king.
Back in Thelanis, the gnomes there also grew in power. They came to control one of their own feyspires: Pyras Pyiral. This feyspire manifested in Zilargo.
Subspecies: Deep Gnome
Most Gnomes are petite, with big eyes and pointed ears. They often have similar features to humans and halflings.Gnomes have an innate thirst for knowledge, and are known to always ask questions. They often use diplomacy, but are not above blackmail or espionage either. They frequently keep their knowledge to themselves, and hide emotions from others. Family and clan is most important to gnomes, and are typically the only others a gnome will trust.

item.title: Great Druid Oalian
item.description:
Infobox
Oalian is the high leader of The Wardens of the Wood, and essentially Eldeen Reaches.
The people of the Eldeen Reaches were once drawn to the area by a mysterious voice. Thus findind Oalian, who taught them the ways of the wild and the duties of the Gatekeepers. Eventually his students started to develop different ideas, thus forming their own druidic sects.
Activities: Oalian is unmoving, spending his time in Greenheart. He speaks to those who choose to listenPersonality: Oalian is wise, having been the first tree ever awakened.

item.title: Oalian
Ulara d'Jorasco
item.description:
Infobox
Ulara d'Jorasco is the Baron and house Matriarch to House Jorasco. She is also the leader of Resthold, the Healers Guild enclave and training hospital in Vedykar, Karrnath.
Activities: Ulara spends most of her time at the House Jorasco headquarters in Vedykar and governs the house from there. While shes hardly a recluse, she only leaves her villa when necessary and rarely travels far from Resthold. She delegates most day-to-day affairs of enclaves across Khorvaire to her younger family members, and manages affairs through intermediaries and delegates as needed. Advisors and House officials are often seen streaming in and out of her villa all day long. She doesn't pay much attention to the traditional Talenta Halflings of the Talenta Plains.
Personality: Ulara has little interest in politics in comparison to the other Dragonmark Houses.

item.title: Halfling
item.description:
Col Halflings are tribal humanoids originating from the eastern coast of Khorvaire. These halflings have been known to produce livestock while riding atop dinosaurs.

All halflings hail from the Talenta Plains, as they were native to the eastern lands of Khorvaire. They were split into nomadic tribes, moving across the land constantly by dinosaur. Each tribe had an appointed lath, chosen by merit.
Most modern halflings follow their ancestral roots and still live a nomadic life. However, some halflings have migrated to other parts of Khorvaire, leading a more urban lifestyle.
Halflings have the same features as humans, but half the size. The average height of a halfling is 3'10"- 4'2". They typically weigh 75-85 lbs. Most halflings, especially Talenta Halflings, wear a hunt-mask, a symbol of their tribe and especially their bonded connection to their mount.Talenta Halflings tend to be weary of strangers, as their lands are often raided. They do not trust easy, and often have xenophobic tendencies. However, Urban Halflings are usually more open, most having no ties to their Talenta ancestries.
Lathon Halpum: Tribal leader for multiple tribes in the Talenta Plains.

item.title: halfling
Aasimar
item.description:
Col Aasimars are the descendants of humans and celestial bloodlines. This race is very rare on the world of Eberron. They often live amongst other races, and have a wide array of looks based off of their celestial parent.

Aasimars are children of a Human and celestial bloodline. Their ancestors can be one of a multitude of races from one of many planes.
Homeland: Aasimar can be found on both Khorvaire and Sarlona.Aasimar are often tall, attractive, and usually have subtle celestial traits such as golden eyes or silver hair. Of course the celestial traits often depend on the celestial ancestry.
Generally good aligned. Much like Paladins, Aasimar fight in favor of their celestial ancestor. They tend to live in isolation, however some have been known to integrate into society.
Prince Lorrister of the Heavenly Fleet

item.title: Angel
item.description:
Col Angels are a race of celestial that fight on the side of good. They exist on various planes. When angels become corrupted, they are cast out by their brethren, ripped of their wings and damned to the Material Plane. These angels become radiant idols who serve the cause of evil. They often seek revenge on their brethren.

Angels have been known to hail from multiple planar regions, such as Irian, Shavarath, and Syrania. They serve the cause of Sovereign Host, however they do not have direct access to the words of their lords. Some angels serve the Church of the Silver Flame, and can be found in Flamekeep.Angels are the peak of flawless beauty. Most angels stand taller than mortals at 9'. They possess a variety of skin and hair colors. They have feathery wings that sprout from their shoulders. Angels may appear differently depending on their homeland. Deva: Divine Messengers Planetars: Divine Warriors Solars: Most powerful angels with godlike abilities. Angels are paragons of virtue, honor, and honesty. They are trustworthy diplomats. Angels do not wish violence, but will engage quickly if the need arises.
'Vyrael, The Guardian of the portal between Syrania and Sharn.

item.title: Archon
item.description:
Col Archons are celestial beings who fight the endless battle for good against demons and devils.
Archons, similar to angels, are planar forces of good. The main difference being that archons are not afraid to do what they have to in the name of good. Archons strive to end the demonic control that consumes Shavarath.
During The Last War, in the year 983 YK, Thrane summoned four archons to spearhead their Great Eastern Campaign. These archons, named the Messengers, each led a separate division:
the Army of the Ascended
the Righteous Legion
the Legion of True Brethren
The Army of the Eastern Crusade
Each archon commanded roughly 10,000 troops. The archons led Thrane to take the cities of Eston and Kalazart. However, upon obtaining large trunks of books and scrolls, the forces withdrew to Flamekeep, and the Messengers vanished. Varies between species:
Hound Archon
Lantern Archon
Archons are very similar to angels. They tend to forego honor and virtue in the name of good.
Prince Lorrister of the Heavenly Fleet

item.title: Azer
item.description:
Col Azer are fiery, Dwarf-like creatures native to the plane of Fernia.

Azers are primarily weaponsmiths, working with primal elements to create unique weapons. They can primarily be found on Fernia, but can also be spotted on the volcanic fields of Xen'drik.Azers very closely resemble dwarves, but with flames instead of hair/beards. They have brass colored skin that almost appears forged. They tend to dress in brass, copper, or bronze.Azer are a generally reserved species, very dedicated to their work. However they will fight if provoked. They love gemstones, and will fight to the death if enraged in combat.

item.title: Bugbear
item.description:
Col A massive humanoid distantly related to goblins and hobgoblins. They are one of the only goblinoids to be covered in fur. Like many goblinoids, bugbears were once part of the dominant civilization of Khorvaire thousands of years ago.

Bugbear are believes to have originated during the rise of the Dhakaani Empire, bred by the hobgoblins to serve as slaves and elite soldiers. After the dissolution of the Dhakaani Empire, bugbear continued to be ruled by the hobgoblins in tribes known as the Ghaal'dar. Some bugbear rebelled, seizing the land by the Seawall Mountains anf forming their own tribes. These tribes became known as the "Marguul", or warrior kings.
Now, some of the Marguul pay homage to Lhesh Haruuc, while others continue to fight Haruuc's forces, vowing to never bow to a Hobgoblin again.
Otherwise, bugbear can be found in small numbers across Khorvaire, and often live peacefully.Bugbear resemble hairy, beastly goblins standing at 7 ft. tall. Their noses and claws share a resemblance to bears, hence the name. They typically weigh in between 200-450 lbs.Bugbear tend to have a truthful reputation of being dim-witted and brutish. In their societies, they tend to value violence among themselves.

item.title: Bullywug
item.description:
Col Bullywugs, a race of froglike humaniods present on the east coast of Khorvaire

Bullywug are native to the eastern coast of Khorvaire, particularly the warmer regions, such as the Lhazaar Principalities. Their ancestors were supposedly once humans or goblinoids transformed by a god called the Lord of the Murky Waters. They are known for their ancient conflict with the Lizardfolk.Bullywug are amphibious humanoids that stand between 5'4"-6' and weigh 150 to 240 lbs.
Bullywug can often be seen as cruel and aggressive, especially in the Trub Glorp tribe, which brought them to conflict with humans. These creatures tend to ruin any land they come across, even their own swamps. However, they do not appear to be unaware of this phenomenon. The difference in environment can create a sense of self-doubt and paranoia, thinking everything is out to get them. Some bullywug have been documented to resorting to cannibalism, however some cannibalize by choice.

item.title: Drow
item.description:
Col A race of Elves who live on Xen'drik

Like all other elves, drow were former slaves of the Giants, but remained in Xen'drik after the Giants civilization collapsed. The three main cultural groups of drow are the Vulkoori, the Sulatar, and the Umbragen.
Drow are generally dark-skinned, and smaller and thinner than other elves. Drow can often have vivid red eyes. Their hair color can vary from white to other pale shades, such as grey, silver, or white-gold. Female drow are slightly larger than male drow.Varies between tribes.

item.title: Elf
item.description:
Col A race of graceful humaniods known for their long lifespans.
Elves of Eberron are descended from the Eladrin of the feyspire city of Shae Tirias Tolai.
During the Age of Giants, the city was ransacked by the giants of Xen'drik and its inhabitants were enslaved. This enslavement changed the Eladrin into the elves we know today, and allowed them to learn magic from the giants. After the fall of this civilization, many elves fled to the continent Aerenal.
During the Age of Monsters, some of the elves of Aerenal departed to Khorvaire and settled in modern day Valenar. This colony was later abandoned, but during The Last War, elves mercenaries of the Valaes Tairn cited this as justification for founding the nation of Valenar.Elves can vary in skin, hair, and eye color. They are usually taller, 5'6"- 6'5" ft tall, but only 150-190lbs. They have long, pointed ears and usually long, elegant features.
Elves in Eberron are known to be strange and diverse people. The elves who live in Khorvaire have integrated into society, and now have similar culture and identity.
High King Shaeras Vadallia: War leader of the Valaes Tairn and the head of state of Valenar.
Balaereth and Tezaera Mendyrian: Current Sibling Kings of Aerenal
Baron Elvinor Elorrenthi d'Phiarlan: Current Matriarch of House Phiarlan.
Baron Elar d'Thuranni: Current Patriarch of House Thuranni.
Maza ir'Thadian: Only current elven member of the Sharn city council.
Syraen Melideth: Governor of Pylas Talaear.
Mordain the Fleshweaver: Former wizard of The Twelve and member of House Phiarlan.

item.title: Goblin
item.description:
Col Native to the continent of Khorvaire

Goblins are native to Khorvaire, and were originally united under the Dhakaani Empire 16,000 years ago. Eventually the Daelkyr weakened the Empire, causing collapse. Many goblins became part of disunited clans led by hobgoblins. When the first humans landed on Khorvaire, the goblins were enslaved and used to build cities. This practice was ended by Galifar ir'Wynarn I. Many goblins have flat faces, broad noses, pointed ears, and small, sharp fangs. They have sloped back foreheads, and their eyes can vary from yellow to red. Their skin color ranges from yellow, through orange, to red, and even green. Usually members of the same tribe share similar colors.Goblins are nimble and elusive, often working in the shadows. They typically don't have high morals, and protect their kind to no end.

item.title: Half-Elf (Khoravar)
item.description:
Col As they originate from Khorvaire, half evles call themselves Khoravar.

Khoravar are a race created by the interbreeding of elves and humans. Two khoravar houses are known to have dragonmark bloodlines: House Lyrandar and House Medani.
Khoravar can have any color skin, hair, eyes, or other attributes. They often have half elven ears, and share other features common between humans and elves. They average 5'5"-6'2", and 130-190lbs.Like their ancestors, Khoravar can have any type of personality, alignment, or goals.

item.title: Harpy
item.description:
Col A monstrous humanoid creature known for its entrancing voice and ability to fly.
Harpies have inhabited the Byeshk Mountains since before the Dhakaani Empire. They have been known to serve the Daughters of Sora Kell.
The harpys have their own type of settlements, known as Flights:Flights
Brass Talons
Carrion Callers
Crimson Wind
Forgotten Choir
Haunting Song
Last Chants
Last Dirge
Rotwings
Stormsingers
Wind Howlers
In the face, harpies actually resemble elves. However, they sproud ugly, birdlike wings. Harpies also have several other birdlike creatures, typically clawed feet and hands, but can also be seen having almost beaks, or bird feet.Harpies are notoriously malicious, evil and sadistic. They are fond of entrancing travelers with their enchanting song, only to torture and savor their victims. They are not particularly intelligent, and have been noted to cower in the face of supreme power.
Callian of the Bloody Word: leader of the Wind Howlers, actively stands again the Daughters of Sora Kell.
Cazha Bloodwing: member of the criminal organization, Daask.
Jalira Stormtongue: member of the Flayer Guard, and commander of a squad of harpies and gargoyles for the Guard.
Sklar: a former associate of Sora Teraza.
Zoryanna of the Last Dirge: manager of the Venomous Voice, an in at Graywall.

item.title: Hobgoblin
item.description:
Col One of the original races of Khorvaire known as ghaal'dar or "mighty people" in their own language.

Goblin Kingdom leaders in Khorvaire about 38,000 years ago, at the beginning of the Age of Monsters. 16,000 years ago, the clans of Dhakaani organized the kingdoms to create the Dhakaani Empire. After the fall of the Dhakaani Empire, the hobgoblins split into two tribes: Ghaal'dar and the Heirs of Dhakaan.
Similar appearance to a Goblin, but much larger and more powerful.
Hobgoblins are notable fighters, often being recruited as soldiers or mercenaries. The Ghaal'dar pick more fights, while the Heirs of Dhakaan tend to strategize in the shadows more.
Llesh Haruuc Shaarat'kor: Ruler of Darguun
Kreldo: Fortune Teller in Stormreach
Margaash: Mercenary captain of Sharn
Vhuklok Vant: A magistrate for the Tribunal of Thronehold representing Darguun.

item.title: Lantern Archon
item.description:
Col Lantern Archons exist in the plane of Irian. These archons are the "youngest" archons, as they are recent souls of good and lawfulness that have died in the Material Plane. These little guys mostly offer aid in times of need.
Lantern Archons are the most recently passed souls of lawful and good. Lanterns are small, floating balls of light. They are about as bright as a torch, and emit a soft glow.It is misconstrued that Lanterns lack a sense of intelligence or wisdom as they lack a material body. However, this is not the truth. They speak in soft, musical voices and do whatever they can to help those in need.

item.title: Hound Archon
item.description:
Col A species of Archon found on the plane of Shavarath

Hound Archons prowl the Shavarath plane battlefield, destroying any devils and demons that they encounter.Hound Archons take a humaniod body, with a hound-like face. Like humans, they wear clothing. And while most prefer to use their claws and fangs, others wield greatswords and other weapons.Generally good aligned. Always willing to do what they need to do to destroy the evil and chaos plaguing the land. These archons are true champions of justice.

item.title: The Gloaming
item.description:
The Gloaming is the darkest part of the Towering Wood in the Eldeen Reaches. This region acts as a manifest zone for Mabar. The beaut and splendor of this part of the forest changes into a parasite-infested land, concealing monstrous insects and undead in the twisted and malformed trees.
The Gloaming is located in the southern part of the Towering Wood. This region is about 15mi and is separated into three 5mi rings, with the middle intersection being the most powerful of the zone.
Over the past century, The Gloaming has been slowly expanding. The Children of Winter used to dwell in this area, studying the expansion. However, most left since the Day of Mourning.
Some believe that the Gloaming is a result of the Daelkyr. Although the Children of Winter say it is a sign of what is to come, a serpent of legacy infused with the power of the Gloaming, named Coldfang. However, some scholars believe the Gloaming is a possible origin of Lycanthropy.
While the Children of Winter have mostly abandoned this region, some have returned to the southern sector to ward off intruders.
Members of the Ashbound druid sect often navigate the borders of the Gloaming, picking fights with the Children of Winter.
The Nightbringers, an offshoot of the Children of Winter, reside deep in the inner ring of the Gloaming, studying the influence of Mabar.

The Twelve
item.description:
The Board of Dragonmarks
The Twelve were an organization of wizards that sponsored each dragonmarked house to keep the houses in order.
This organization was formed after the War of the Mark in an alliance proposed by Lord Hadran d'Cannith to unify the houses in pursuing magical research and profit.
Since The Last War, the power of the individual dragonmarked houses and the Arcane Congress has caused The Twelve to diminish and end.
The Twelve mainly based out of The Twelve Tower above Karrnath. However they were known to have many secret enclaves and fortresses.As much exploration and experimentation The Twelve participated in, they were most known for training members and apprentices in arcane magic.
The Twelve was very focused on both magical and technological advancements. They used their union to assist each other in various advancements. There are rumors of a secret conspiracy to take over Khorvaire, and to oppose the Dragons of Argonnessen.
The AD was the arm of The Twelve that would explore for rare magic. These members have been known to steal treasures from the Wayfinder Foundation under "Project Reclamation"

item.title: Elf
Siberys
item.description:
Siberys was one of the Progenitor Dragons, who was unfortunately slain by his sister, Khyber. Scattered across the dark void, his scales became the glittering stars seen now across the sky of Eberron. At night, you can see a ring of golden stars surrounding the world, called The Ring of Siberys.
After the slaughter of Siberys and the binding of Khyber, the blood of Siberys, the body of Eberron became alive, and created the first Dragons. Some of this blood did not rain upon the world, and thus granted life to his own creatures, the Coatls.
As his life force faded from the fabric of the cosmosis, Siberys became the force of magic which permeates everything. It is said that he is the reason why magic is available to all races, especially Dragons.
